issue.title: Tighten sase stitch create --resume's identity check beyond subject-only matching

task_type_fields.proposal: Stop sase stitch create --resume from finalizing a commit it did not create. Today the only identity gate is a subject-line comparison (workflow_resume.py:63-78); add a check that HEAD is a commit this run is entitled to finalize — primarily that HEAD is not already reachable from the upstream tracking branch, optionally that HEAD still touches the checkpointed diff's paths — and abort with HEAD unpushed and recoverable when it is not. Keep the check advisory enough not to break legitimate conflict resolutions that change content.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Specified in epic sase-p5's plan under phase restamp but never implemented, and outside sase-p5's goal statement, which is scoped to the commit finalizer's discarded-work guard no longer failing agents whose work landed. This addresses the opposite risk — silently finalizing an unrelated commit — and the defect (subject-only matching) predates the epic. It also needs a new VCS-agnostic upstream-containment primitive across the provider protocol, git plugin, and test fakes, which is more than a landing cleanup.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-p5 / sase-p5.1 — the proposing epic and phase. sase-p5.1 (commit 22e5444bf) implemented the footer restamp from the same plan section but not this identity tightening; read plan:202608/commit_finalizer_attribution.md, section 'Make the SASE commit footer survive conflict resolution', for the original specification and its warning to keep the check advisory.

RELATED: sase-ln — 'sase stitch create's _stage_all_except swept a concurrent agent's uncommitted work into an unrelated commit, already pushed to origin/master'. Adjacent failure mode in the same command: that one commits work the run does not own, this one finalizes a commit the run did not create. Worth reading for how that fix scoped ownership.
